name: Ouroboros Risk Analytics Field Blazer
manufacturer: Ouroboros Internal Procurement, Halcyon Tailoring Division
description:
Ouroboros's field-facing analysts — the ones who visit sites after accidents, assess claims, and make the quiet determinations that decide whether families get paid — wear this blazer as part of their mandatory client-contact uniform. Cut in a slim, androgynous silhouette from a wool-polyamide blend that holds its press through a 14-hour shift, the jacket comes in two approved colors: deep navy and a warm charcoal. The Ouroboros ouroboros-snake logo is embroidered on the left breast in thread that shifts from gold to silver depending on the viewing angle, a subtle flex that clients in Tier 2 and 3 zones always notice.

The fabric contains a passive environmental sensor mesh that logs temperature, air quality, and ambient radiation — officially for the analyst's safety, practically to build a data record Ouroboros can use in claim disputes. Collar and cuff cuts are standard and not particularly aug-friendly, but the jacket is produced in 40 body configurations including tail-accommodating rear vents and extended shoulder clearance for wing stubs. Analysts are required to maintain the blazer in pristine condition; visible wear is grounds for uniform replacement fees deducted from the next pay cycle.
cultural_context: When an Ouroboros blazer shows up at your door or workplace, something has gone wrong for someone. The uniform carries the weight of institutional power — polite, well-dressed, and absolutely not on your side. Some Ouroboros analysts hate what the uniform represents. Most have learned not to think about it.
story_hooks: An analyst discovers the environmental sensor mesh in her blazer has been logging data that directly contradicts the official report she was told to file.
A blazer belonging to a missing Ouroboros field analyst surfaces in a Tier 1 pawn shop — still transmitting location data to Ouroboros servers.
A Tier 2 community organizer gets hold of an authentic Ouroboros blazer and uses it to bluff her way into a corporate claims hearing.

physical_description.visual_profile: A precisely cut slim blazer that reads as institutional authority — structured shoulders, clean lines, androgynous silhouette that projects professionalism and detachment. The kind of garment that makes people uncomfortable just by entering a room.
physical_description.fit: Slim, tailored cut through the torso with minimal taper at the waist. Designed to accommodate standard humanoid frames across 40 body configurations including non-human anatomy (tail vents, shoulder clearance for augments). Length hits mid-hip. Cuffs and collar cut standard, not augment-accommodating.
physical_description.primary_material: Wool-polyamide blend with integrated passive environmental sensor mesh woven into the weave. Fabric holds press for extended wear cycles without wrinkle recovery.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, structured wool surface with imperceptible sensor mesh beneath. Feels expensive and cold to touch. Fabric has slight grip — designed to maintain form and not wrinkle under 14+ hour shifts.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep navy or warm charcoal gray as only approved options. Left breast features an embroidered ouroboros snake logo in iridescent thread (gold-to-silver shift depending on angle). No other pattern or ornamentation.
physical_description.closures: Standard button front (likely concealed under placket for clean lines). No magnetic snaps or friction-fit — pure corporate formality.
distinctive_features: Iridescent ouroboros logo on left breast — shifts gold/silver, signals institutional affiliation
Rear vents accommodating tails or alternative anatomies
Integrated passive environmental sensor mesh logging temperature, air quality, radiation
Pristine fabric finish with zero distressing — wear is a uniform code violation
Androgynous cut across multiple body configurations
Halcyon Tailoring Division manufacturing tag (visible when uniform is replaced)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional / institutional. The uniform itself marks the wearer as corporate-adjacent, not wealthy elite. The cost of replacement for visible wear signals precarity — analysts pay penalties for damage.
physical_description.cultural_context: Ouroboros Risk Analytics field agent. When this blazer appears, a claim denial or institutional investigation is likely underway. Worn by people whose job is to arrive at disaster scenes, assess suffering, and determine who gets paid. The uniform is a barrier — polite, professional, impenetrable. Wearing it means you've chosen (or been forced into) institutional authority over human connection.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine or replaced. Code violations result in pay deductions. Analysts obsess over keeping it perfect because the alternative is financial penalty. Paradoxically, the blazer's perfection makes it more sinister — no wear, no humanity, just cold procedure.
